certified.title: Certified Translation
certified.description: Translations signed by registered public translators, accepted by immigration offices, courts, universities, and public institutions.
documents: Criminal record checks and immigration documents
Documents for Italian or Spanish citizenship
certified.customers: People applying for citizenship, a visa, or degree recognition, international students, HR teams, and law firms.
certified.whySpecialists: Every seal, stamp, and annotation must be reproduced completely and precisely. Whether you need a passport, a diploma, a university degree, or a birth certificate translated, our public translators know the exact format each authority requires.

legal.title: Legal Translation
legal.description: Documents translated with precise terminology and legal equivalence between systems.
legal.customers: Law firms, in-house counsel, notaries, and government bodies.
legal.whySpecialists: One imprecise clause can shift liability or void an agreement. Legal translators preserve the exact force of the source text within the target legal system.

medical.title: Medical Translation
medical.description: Two languages, two healthcare systems — only one way to read it right.
medical.customers: Hospitals, clinics, research organizations, and pharmaceutical companies.
medical.whySpecialists: Patient safety depends on unambiguous language. Our medical translators work with clinical and regulatory terminology every day.

technical.title: Technical Translation
technical.description: We build a glossary and translation memory for each client, so the same term is always translated the same way.
technical.customers: Manufacturers, engineering firms, and mining and energy companies.
technical.whySpecialists: A mistranslated tolerance or warning label is a safety risk. Technical translators keep units, terminology, and procedures exact from source to target.

business.title: Business & Financial Translation
business.description: Financial disclosure language is regulated. Our translators keep figures and terms in every language.

localization.title: Website & Software Translation
localization.description: Adapted to your target language and market.

transcription.title: Transcription & Subtitling
transcription.description: Subtitling isn’t translation. It’s fitting, timing and keeping every word that matters.
documents: videos for YouTube and social media
transcription.customers: Production companies, marketing and training teams, researchers, and law firms.
transcription.whySpecialists: Accents, crosstalk, and background noise decide how long an hour of audio really takes. Subtitles have to be cut into readable lines and timed to the picture.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions

cost.question: How much does a translation cost?
cost.answer: It depends on the word count, the language pair, the subject area, and the deadline. Each project is quoted differently: documents by word, certificates by page, transcription and subtitling by minute of audio or video.

turnaround.question: How long does it take?
turnaround.answer: Ten pages usually takes 24 to 48 hours. For bigger projects, we send you a delivery schedule along with the quote.

confidentiality.question: How do you keep my documents confidential?
confidentiality.answer: Files are transferred over encrypted connections and access is limited to the professionals assigned to your project.

payment.question: What payment methods do you accept?
payment.answer:
Argentina: transfer to Mercado Pago or to a Banco Santander Argentina account.
Chile: transfer to a Banco de Chile or Banco Santander Chile account.
Peru: Plin or transfer to a Banco Interbank account.
All countries: crypto (wallet transfer or Binance Pay).

revisions.question: Can I ask for changes after delivery?
revisions.answer: Of course — just get in touch and we’ll make the changes.

rush.question: Do you offer expedited translation services?
rush.answer: Let us know your deadline in your quote request, we will confirm availability immediately.

legalization.question: Does the translation come legalized?
legalization.answer:
No. Legalization and the apostille are personal procedures for the document holder. We deliver the translation signed and ready for that step, which depends on the country.
Argentina: a registered public translator (traductor público matriculado) signs it; you have the signature legalized at the Colegio de Traductores and, if the destination requires it, apostilled.
Peru: a sworn public translator (traductor público juramentado) or a certified member translator (traductor colegiado certificado) signs it; you have the signature legalized or apostilled at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Chile: there is no public translator figure, so a professional translator signs it. If the receiving institution requires the official translation from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, we obtain it for you.
Before translating: if the original document needs legalization or an apostille, that step comes first.
